rfm_tuples.R: "During the year ended December 31, 2025, we recognized asset impairment charges of $141.0 million associated with manufacturer franchise rights ... compared to $149.5 million ... during the year ended December 31, 2024."
rfm_tuples.f: Verify trend of recurring non-cash impairments across years; check whether this is a one-time event or chronic.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Three-year impairment history: 2025 $141.0M, 2024 $149.5M, 2023 $117.2M. Cumulative $407.7M over three years — i.e., management is consistently overpaying for franchise rights in M&A (LHM 2021, Koons 2023, Herb Chambers 2025) and writing them down annually. This is a recurring, not episodic, charge.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Disclosure is honest (charges are quantified and the audit committee disclosed them as a critical audit matter), but the chronic nature of the impairments indicates an M&A engine that systematically overstates synergies. Not fraud — the issuer is transparent. But the franchise-rights asset base ($1B+) remains at risk and 2026 could see another round given the underperforming stores cited in Note 7.

rfm_tuples.M_value: FY2025 same-store new vehicle units +3%, but same-store new vehicle gross profit -8% (-$49M) on margin compression. Same-store used vehicle revenue -4% (-$185M). FY2025 reported net-income growth +14% to $492M is driven by a $80.2M divestiture gain + Herb Chambers contribution + lower impairment, not organic. Q1 2026 is starker: same-store new vehicle revenue -9% (-$187M); same-store domestic new vehicle gross profit -31%; Q1 income from operations -17%; SG&A +12% ($54M). Reported Q1 net income +42% to $187.8M ONLY because of a $125.8M divestiture gain — backing it out, pre-tax income ex-divestiture is ~$125M vs $171M Q1'25 (-27%).
rfm_tuples.interpretation: The reported headline numbers are 'good' but the underlying organic business is in moderate decline (used vehicle softness, new vehicle margin normalization, SG&A creep from Herb Chambers integration). Issuer discloses the divestiture gain prominently — not deceptive, but the gap between headline EPS and same-store operating EPS is material and likely explains some of the drawdown.

rfm_tuples.M_value: Current maturities of long-term debt jumped from $114.7M (2024) to $479.2M (2025). Aggregate maturity schedule: 2026 $484.4M, 2027 $42.4M, 2028 $610.2M, 2029 $837.7M. The 2026 maturity is dominated by the 2021 Real Estate Facility ($442.1M balloon, 5-yr from Dec 17, 2021 = due Dec 2026). Total debt $3.59B, leverage drifted from 2.9x → 3.2x (above target 2.5-3.5x range, near top). $1.57B floor plan facility on top. Q1 2026: all covenants compliant. Refinancing the $442M RE facility at higher rates than 2021 (when SOFR was ~0%) will pressure interest expense — already +5% YoY in 2025 ($187.5M total other interest).
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Leverage is within target but at the high end after Herb Chambers, and the $442M 2026 RE-facility balloon is the most concrete near-term risk. Issuer discloses this transparently in the maturity table. Not severe — ABG has revolver capacity ($925M total, only $120M drawn at 12/31/25 = ~$780M unused), liquidity is intact, and they generated $492M of net income with $80M+ of divestiture cash. But the refi at 5-6% SOFR vs 1.55% spread originally will compress earnings and is part of the drawdown narrative.

summary: ABG is a -29% drawdown name where the FORENSIC tape directly REJECTS the SHORT thesis: CEO David Hult put $1.03M of personal cash into open-market purchases on 2026-03-06 (post-Q4 print), independent director DiSantis added at $202 in March AND $182 in May (scaling in through the bottom), and 10%+ holder Abrams Capital absorbed $10.6M of stock at $225 after the Herb Chambers deal. P:S ratio 11.6x with ZERO CEO/CFO sales in 12 months. Business is honestly disclosed as moderately impaired (recurring ~$140M annual franchise-rights impairments, -9% same-store new-vehicle revenue in Q1'26, integration drag from Herb Chambers driving SG&A +12%, $442M Real Estate Facility balloon maturing Dec 2026) but covenants are clean, leverage 3.2x within target range, EY clean opinion, $780M revolver unused. Reported earnings flatter the underlying organic decline via divestiture gains ($80M FY25, $126M Q1'26), so headline 'growth' overstates true operating trend — but issuer discloses these line-items transparently, no fraud or accounting deception. Verdict: LONG-tier. The insider-vs-narrative test is the strongest signal Signal OS can produce and ABG is the clearest insider-conviction setup in the forward-test universe. Severity: 4 PASS / 5 MODERATE / 0 SEVERE / 0 RED_FLAG / 0 UNVERIFIABLE.
